name: New Hampshire

statute.name: Right-to-Know Law (Access to Government Records and Meetings)

response.rule_text: Within 5 business days agency must make the record available, deny in writing with reasons, or acknowledge in writing and state the time reasonably necessary (RSA 91-A:4, IV).

fees.copy_rule: Actual cost of providing the copy when a public device is used (RSA 91-A:4, IV).
fees.late_penalty: Attorney fees if body knew or should have known of violation (RSA 91-A:8, I).

residency.rule_text: Statute refers to every citizen (91-A:4), all persons (91-A:2), any person (91-A:7); RCFP reads this as no residency limit.

appeal.rule_text: No agency appeal; requester may complain to the Ombudsman or petition Superior Court (91-A:7); filing in court bars later ombudsman complaint. No deadline stated by RCFP.

format_rule: Electronic copies in standard or common file formats or printouts (RSA 91-A:4, V); no customized searches or new records required (91-A:4, VII).
notes: Governor covered only when acting with Executive Council. Legislature covered by definition (91-A:1-a, VI(a)) but conference committee held not subject (Hughes 2005). Universities: USNH trustees covered. Appeal type chosen court though ombudsman option exists. RCFP summary partially updated Sept 2023. First 100k chars read.
